messages.subject: Re: Consideration of batch and gender effects
messages.subject_clean: Consideration of batch and gender effects
messages.body_plain:
Hi Juan,

This is a nice design! Since your sample allocation balances disease and gender in every batch, you avoided confounding between these factors and the batch. The ‘global’ normalization with MSstats will account for systematic changes between the batches that affect all the proteins. The analysis with MSstats without any extra adjustments will not be subject to the confounding bias.

You can choose to extend the analysis by accounting for the batch and gender effects at the level of individual proteins. This will reduce the estimated standard errors and increase the sensitivity. However, since the number of replicates in each combination of batch/condition/gender is relatively small, this will introduce the risk of overfitting (and false positives).

If you decide to do the adjustments, you implement this by creating a new ‘condition’, which is a combination of all the levels of disease.gender.batch (i.e., 8 total). Then create a contrast where you compare two diseases on average over all genders and batches. This will effectively perform the adjustment.

Btw, regardless of what you do, do not include in the MSstats analysis the ’total pool’ samples. Since they represent multiple individuals (as opposed to one individual at a time), they do not have the same structure of variation as the rest of the samples, and will not be well represented by the model.

HTH
Olga

messages.subject: Re: MSstatsPTM site collapse
messages.body_plain:
Hi Klemens,

The unmodified site A0A0G2L974 is most likely there because it was in the PTM dataset before modeling. I.E. MSstatsPTM will model all the unique names in the "Protein" column that goes into the modeling function. It should not be there and is a result of the upstream data processing leaving in unmodified peptides.

In terms of multiple modification sites, MSstatsPTM assumes the identified sites the user uploads are correct. It does not do any site validation or localization. In your case there are two separate models, one for the single modification site S579 and one for the doubly modified S579 and S597. We use features with only the single modification S579 in the single modification model and use only features with both S579 and S597 in the doubly modified model. We do not try to parse out the effect of individual PTMs at this time.

I hope this makes sense.

Devon

Hi Sudip,

The `groupcomparisonPTM` function outputs three models: unadjusted PTM, global protein, and adjusted PTM. The unadjusted PTM and global protein are modeled independently, and the adjusted PTM model is the PTM model after accounting for changes in the overall protein. You do not need to process anything separately, MSstatsPTM will do it all for you. The manuscript  <https://www.mcponline.org/article/S1535-9476(22)00285-7/fulltext>goes into the methods and implementation in more detail.

The quantification function from MSstats will work, you just need to run it on the PTM and Protein separately (i.e. quantification(summary.data$PTM) and quantification(summary.data$PROTEIN)). There is no direct way to filer rows in MSstats, you would need to do a custom filtering to determine this.

Hope this helps!

Devon

> Hi Juan,
>
> This is a nice design! Since your sample allocation balances disease and gender in every batch, you avoided confounding between these factors and the batch. The ‘global’ normalization with MSstats will account for systematic changes between the batches that affect all the proteins. The analysis with MSstats without any extra adjustments will not be subject to the confounding bias.
>
> You can choose to extend the analysis by accounting for the batch and gender effects at the level of individual proteins. This will reduce the estimated standard errors and increase the sensitivity. However, since the number of replicates in each combination of batch/condition/gender is relatively small, this will introduce the risk of overfitting (and false positives).
>
> If you decide to do the adjustments, you implement this by creating a new ‘condition’, which is a combination of all the levels of disease.gender.batch (i.e., 8 total). Then create a contrast where you compare two diseases on average over all genders and batches. This will effectively perform the adjustment.
>
> Btw, regardless of what you do, do not include in the MSstats analysis the ’total pool’ samples. Since they represent multiple individuals (as opposed to one individual at a time), they do not have the same structure of variation as the rest of the samples, and will not be well represented by the model.

messages.body_plain:
Dear MSstats Team

I'm sorry to once more bother you with a question regarding the global median normalization process of MSstats. I have a dataset with a generally high proportion of missing values (~50% at feature level) and a sample (#9, blue square), which in addition had some issues during sample prep, hence most proteins are missing (and I agree, that therefore this particular sample or even dataset should be excluded from further analysis).
Nevertheless, I don't understand why the global median normalization wasn't applied for sample #9 (in contrast to the other samples) and its median remained close to zero. Is there something like a threshold applied (e.g. more50missing)?
Furthermore, I always assumed that the censored values are not taken into account for normalization, hence I don't understand why the interquartile range of the ABUNDANCE values starts close to zero for samples #1,2,3,4,5,8 with a perfectly aligned median. If you filter out all the censored values (right panel), the IQR looks fine again, but the median doesn't align anymore with the other samples (e.g. sample #2, red square).
To me, it looks like the censored values ARE used for normalization. If this is true, could you quickly explain the rationale behind this, 'cause these values will be replaced with the imputed ones in the next step anyway... (I've also tried maxQuantileforCensored = 0.99 to make sure that all missing values (values =< 1) are censored)

I was using MSstats 4.6.3 and following settings for processing the data:

ms_raw <- SpectronauttoMSstatsFormat(input = SNdata,
                                     annotation = annotation,
                                     intensity = 'PeakArea',
                                     filter_with_Qvalue = TRUE,
                                     qvalue_cutoff = 0.01,
                                     useUniquePeptide = TRUE,
                                     removeFewMeasurements = TRUE,
                                     removeProtein_with1Feature = TRUE,
                                     summaryforMultipleRows = max,
                                     use_log_file = FALSE)

QuantData <- dataProcess(ms_raw,
                         normalization = "equalizeMedians",
                         featureSubset = "topN",
                         n_top_feature = 100,
                         summaryMethod = "TMP",
                         equalFeatureVar = TRUE,
                         censoredInt = "0",
                         MBimpute = TRUE,
                         remove50missing = TRUE,
                         maxQuantileforCensored = 0.999, #also tried with 0.9999 and 0.99 with almost identical results
                         use_log_file = FALSE)

QuantData$FeatureLevelData %>%
    mutate(Log2Int = log2(INTENSITY)) %>%

Dear MSstats Team,

We have been asking for an adapter now also for quite some time and I think that the numbers quite clearly show that DIA-NN is being used more and more:

In 2021 the Nature DIA-NN paper was cited 81 times according to google scholar.
and in 2022 it was cited 227 times
and in 2023 so far it was already cited 66 times suggesting that the number of users quickly increases

Additionally, DIA-NN is a free-to-use software which shows great performance for normal DIA
https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/36609502/

and for Phospho / PTM:
https://pubs.acs.org/doi/10.1021/acs.jproteome.1c00490

We would really appreciate it if the next release of MSstats and MSstatsPTM could contain a supported converter and again I am happy to help if you need any example data / analysis of known datasets with DIA-NN.

Best Klemens
